Mission-Critical Workload
Mission-Critical Workload refers to an application or workload where failure has severe business consequences, requiring the highest levels of reliability, availability, resiliency, and fault tolerance. These workloads must be available continuously—all day, every day—demanding zero-downtime deployments and highly available operations. They are typically significant in scale and complexity, generating high volumes of operational data.

In the context of Microsoft Azure, mission-critical workloads often employ globally distributed, active-active, multi-region deployment designs to maximize resilience. They require effective operational procedures and adherence to operational best practices. Mission-critical workloads form the basis of the Azure Well-Architected series on data platform design, emphasizing principles of high availability, fault tolerance, and reliability.<SEP>A mission-critical workload is a collection of application resources that must be highly reliable, always available, resilient to failures, and operational on the platform.<SEP>A mission-critical workload is a type of workload described in the Well-Architected framework requiring high reliability and security.

Scale Unit
A scale unit is a logical unit or function that can be scaled independently, comprising code components, hosting platforms, deployment stamps, and subscriptions.

Scale-Unit Architecture
Scale-unit architecture is a design pattern that optimizes end-to-end scalability through compartmentalization, allowing logical units to be scaled independently.<SEP>Scale-unit architecture is a design pattern for distributing resources across Azure regions as part of deployment stamps.<SEP>Scale-unit architecture is a design pattern for mission-critical application deployment and scaling.<SEP>A key architectural practice for achieving zero-downtime deployments in mission-critical applications.<SEP>Scale-unit architecture is an application design pattern referenced in the mission-critical architecture documentation.

Azure
Azure is Microsoft's cloud computing platform, providing a wide range of services for hosting, scaling, and managing applications. It offers both Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) solutions, including Virtual Machines and scale sets, across various regions. The platform provides networking, compute, data services, and architecture guidance, with diverse feature sets across languages, SDKs, and APIs, supporting various encryption models.

Azure is designed for deploying and monitoring mission-critical workloads, offering highly available and reliable compute and data platform services. It provides subscriptions and infrastructure services for application deployment within a hyperscale cloud environment.

Separately, "Azure" also refers to a network policy plugin for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) that uses Linux IPTables to enforce specified network policies. This is a distinct component within the broader Azure ecosystem rather than the cloud platform itself.<SEP>Azure is Microsoft's cloud computing platform that provides various services for deploying and managing applications and infrastructure.<SEP>Microsoft Azure is a cloud platform that enables deployment and management of cloud solutions.<SEP>Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform used for hosting mission-critical workloads.<SEP>Microsoft's cloud platform that the Well-Architected Framework guidance is centered on.<SEP>Azure is a cloud platform whose core and native functionalities are leveraged in the maturity model's foundational level.<SEP>Azure is Microsoft's cloud computing platform providing various services and features.

Global Distribution
Global distribution is a strategy for deploying applications across multiple regions in an active/active model to withstand regional and zone failures.<SEP>Global distribution is an application design pattern for deploying across multiple regions.

Deployment Stamp
A deployment stamp is a pattern that covers related components and can be deployed as a regional unit to horizontally scale a solution.<SEP>A deployment stamp is a regional resource deployment that typically corresponds to a scale unit.<SEP>A deployment stamp contains both infrastructure and application layers, treated as ephemeral with a lifecycle tied to a single release.<SEP>A deployment stamp is a regional deployment unit placed in a dedicated subscription so subscription limits apply only within that stamp's context.<SEP>A deployment stamp is an independent regional deployment unit that can be constrained to a single zone or spread across zones for redundancy.

Autoscaling
Autoscaling is the practice of automatically adjusting resource capacity in response to load changes.<SEP>Autoscaling is configured based on service-internal and application-set thresholds to respond to load-level volatility.<SEP>Autoscaling is the Azure-native capability to automatically scale services based on demand, prioritized for services that support it.

Azure Well-Architected Framework
The Azure Well-Architected Framework is a Microsoft guidance framework providing prescriptive architecture best practices for designing, building, and operating high-quality workloads on Microsoft Azure, including mission-critical workloads. It is organized around five core pillars: Reliability (resiliency), Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, and Performance Efficiency.

The framework is structured in a layered approach consisting of pillars, workload guidance, service guides, and design guides, offering actionable architectural decisions and pillar-specific recommendations. It provides comprehensive, cross-pillar design guidance covering application design, platform considerations, scalability, and DevOps practices, along with maturity models and review assessments.

The Azure Well-Architected Framework serves as a set of guiding tenets and principles aimed at driving architectural excellence and improving the overall quality of workloads at the fundamental architectural level.

AKS
AKS (Azure Kubernetes Service) is a managed Kubernetes container orchestration platform on Azure that supports cluster and node management, upgrades, networking, monitoring, and governance. It has scale limits such as 1,000 nodes per cluster and has a hard requirement for an underlying virtual network, requiring network integration configuration with support for Azure CNI and Kubenet networking plugins.

AKS serves as a primary application platform where health endpoints can be configured for pods, and it is monitored for CPU utilization and deployment statuses. It can also be used as a compute platform with services such as Azure Cosmos DB for query-intensive workloads.

Capacity Model
A capacity model defines the scope and relationships between scale units based on performance and non-functional requirements.<SEP>A capacity model is used to monitor data volume, scale limits, and expected growth rates.<SEP>A model enabling planning of resource scale levels for a given load profile and system-wide capacity allocation planning.<SEP>A capacity model quantifies scale relationships between components to ensure automated scale operations encompass all related components.

.NET SDK
The .NET SDK is a software development kit for Azure that provides more capabilities and is updated frequently, prioritized for reliability and performance.

Noisy Neighbor Antipattern
The Noisy Neighbor antipattern occurs when shared resources are consumed disproportionately, and can be avoided by dedicating landing zone subscriptions to specific applications.

Azure Landing Zone
Azure Landing Zone is a foundational platform architecture pattern and pre-configured deployment environment in Azure for deploying applications and resources. It provides Azure policies ensuring consistent reliability and security, and recommends dedicated subscriptions for mission-critical workloads.

Azure Landing Zone offers Online and Corp. Connected variants for different network configurations, providing connectivity to on-premises networks using ExpressRoute or virtual network designs. It serves as a deployment context for integrating with broader organizational network topology following Microsoft best practices.

The architecture supports centralized storage of operational data, allowing data to be forked into both centralized tooling and application-dedicated Log Analytics workspaces. A central platform Log Analytics workspace may need to be queried for platform resource dependencies.<SEP>Azure landing zone provides an additional threat mitigation layer through centralized security capabilities.<SEP>Azure landing zone is a deployment environment that provides network connectivity to on-premises data centers.<SEP>Azure Landing Zone is an environment with centralized baseline policy assignments applied at management group and subscription levels.

Active/Active Model
An active/active deployment strategy that maximizes availability and provides a higher composite SLA by distributing load among all regions.<SEP>The active/active model is a deployment approach where load is distributed among all regions to maximize resilience against regional failures.<SEP>The active/active model is a multi-region deployment strategy strongly recommended for mission-critical workloads where multiple regions run simultaneously.

Microservices Architecture
An architecture style consistent with mission-critical requirements that facilitates high availability by preventing cascading failures.<SEP>Microservices architecture is a style where programming languages and frameworks are optimized at the microservice level.

Azure SDKs
Azure SDKs are software development kits for various programming languages that provide capabilities for building Azure applications.<SEP>Vendor-provided SDKs for connecting to Azure dependent services with built-in resiliency capabilities.

PaaS Services
PaaS (Platform as a Service) services are cloud computing services where legacy or proprietary software might not run.

Java
Java is a programming language with commonly used SDK libraries for Azure that are updated frequently.

Retry
A design pattern that handles transient failures elegantly through cancel, immediate retry, or retry after delay strategies with suitable back-off.<SEP>Retry is a software engineering pattern for handling transient failures in applications.

Circuit Breaker
A design pattern used to implement resiliency in application code for handling failures.<SEP>A design pattern that provides stability by waiting for recovery or quickly rejecting requests rather than blocking while waiting for unavailable remote services.<SEP>Circuit Breaker is a software engineering pattern used to implement resilient applications.

Queue-Based Load Leveling
A design pattern that introduces a buffer between consumers and requested resources to ensure consistent load levels through queued requests processed by worker processes.<SEP>Queue-Based Load Leveling is a software engineering pattern for managing load in cloud applications.

Throttling
A design pattern that controls resource consumption by deferring lower-priority operations when a resource reaches a load threshold.<SEP>Throttling is a software engineering pattern for controlling resource consumption in applications.

Bulkhead
A design pattern that partitions service instances into groups based on load and availability requirements, isolating failures to sustain service functionality.<SEP>Bulkhead is a software engineering pattern for isolating application components to prevent cascading failures.

Saga
A design pattern that manages data consistency across microservices with independent datastores through defined event or message channels and compensating transactions.<SEP>Saga is a software engineering pattern for managing distributed transactions.

Distributed Tracing
A diagnostic technique for end-to-end tracing of requests across services, providing correlation IDs for error messages.<SEP>Distributed tracing is a diagnostic method for tracking requests across microservices.<SEP>Distributed Tracing is a diagnostic concept for tracking requests across distributed systems using correlation IDs.<SEP>Distributed Tracing is facilitated by Application Insights to provide comprehensive error messages with correlation IDs.<SEP>Distributed Tracing is a diagnostic concept for tracking requests across distributed system components.

Health Endpoint Monitoring
A design pattern that implements functional checks in an application accessible through exposed endpoints at regular intervals to inform application health.<SEP>Health Endpoint Monitoring is a pattern for checking the health of application services.

Application Insights
Application Insights is a feature of Azure Monitor that provides application performance monitoring (APM) and distributed tracing capabilities. It serves as a tool for querying, correlating, and visualizing application traces and telemetry data, offering deep insights into application performance.

Application Insights is an Azure Monitor resource that must be deployed and configured to incorporate data collection and querying capabilities. It can be deployed in a workspace-based model underpinned by a Log Analytics workspace. The tool facilitates distributed tracing, telemetry correlation, and provides comprehensive error messages with correlation IDs.

Event-Driven Design
A design approach using asynchronous message processing through an intermediary to build resiliency and support loose coupling.<SEP>Event-driven design is an architecture style referenced for mission-critical application design.

Deployment Stamps
Deployment stamps is an architecture pattern for deploying multiple independent copies of application components.<SEP>Deployment stamps are regional scale units used to distribute workloads across regions or within a single region for fault tolerance.

Azure Expressroute
A connectivity option for accessing workloads through private networks.

Availability Zones
Availability Zones are physically separate locations within an Azure region, each typically corresponding to distinct datacenters. They provide datacenter-level fault tolerance and high availability by distributing resources—such as VMs, AKS control plane and agent nodes, and database replicas—across these separated facilities. The latency between zones is maintained at less than 2 milliseconds.

By spreading workloads across multiple zones, Availability Zones maximize resilience and reliability within a region, ensuring that a failure in one datacenter does not affect resources in another. They offer zone redundancy for services such as Azure Cosmos DB, protecting deployments against zone-level failures while keeping data and compute resources within the same region for low-latency access.<SEP>Infrastructure zones within Azure regions used to distribute solution components for fault tolerance.<SEP>Availability Zones are Azure infrastructure zones that enable 99.99% SLA when Azure Standard Load Balancer is deployed across them.<SEP>Availability Zones are a reliability convention that can be enforced through Azure Policy.<SEP>Availability Zones are used to ensure reliable intra-region deployment configurations for Azure services.<SEP>Availability zones are infrastructure deployments within regions used for reliability, cost, and performance of workloads.

Retries With Backoff
A design pattern for implementing resilient applications by retrying failed operations with exponential backoff.

Loosely Coupled Event-Driven Architecture
An architecture enabling interservice communication via well-defined interfaces where components operate independently using asynchronous messaging.

Health Model
A model that takes corrective action for non-transient failures that cannot be fully mitigated in application logic, informed by application instrumentation and logging.<SEP>A health model defines healthy and unhealthy states for each component to enable fast failure detection and recovery.<SEP>A model used to quantify application health, understand operational efficiency, and identify active threats.<SEP>A health model is an iterative construct used to define and calculate application health through aggregation of resource-level metrics, used in CI/CD pipelines and for SLO attainment.<SEP>The health model is a representation of application health using health probes, structured logging, and visualization with traffic light states.<SEP>The health model is informed by operational data and application instrumentation to facilitate predictive action and troubleshooting.<SEP>A health model represents application health through layered scoring functions, used to drive dashboards and alert rules.

Outbox Pattern
A design pattern used to guarantee consistency so that every message is processed correctly in distributed services.

Transactional Session
A design pattern used alongside Outbox to guarantee data consistency in separate services.

Mission-Critical Application
An application designed to withstand regional and zone failures, maximizing service availability and reliability through resiliency patterns.<SEP>A mission-critical application requires secure, reliable, and scalable ingress traffic with maximum reliability aspirations.

Polly
A proven standardized package for C# that implements resiliency patterns.

Sentinel
A proven standardized package for Java that implements resiliency patterns.<SEP>Sentinel is a security service that, when enabled, extends free data retention in Log Analytics workspace to 90 days.

NServiceBus
A messaging framework with built-in resiliency features.

MassTransit
A messaging framework with built-in resiliency features.

Azure Cosmos DB
Azure Cosmos DB is a globally distributed, highly available NoSQL database service offered by Microsoft Azure. It serves as a primary data platform within many Azure services, designed to store "hot" data actively used by applications and support both transactional and analytical workloads. It is frequently referenced in mission-critical data platform guidance and used as an example of a downstream dependency within regional deployment stamps.

Azure Cosmos DB provides multi-region replication with multi-region write capabilities, making it particularly recommended for applications considering more than four deployment regions. It offers tunable consistency levels, conflict resolution mechanisms, and SLAs for availability and throughput, with configurable failover options supporting high availability. Configurable capabilities include multi-write deployment and periodic backups.

The service supports multiple APIs, including SQL, Cassandra, and MongoDB, and may influence programming language selection due to SDK availability. Core features include partitioning, indexing, autoscale throughput, change feed, built-in Time to Live (TTL) for managing data growth, automatic backups with multiple backup modes, and role-based access control (RBAC) for authentication. Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL specifically provides architecture best practices for globally distributed scenarios.

Azure Cosmos DB also offers an Analytical Store that enables large-scale analytics without impacting transactional performance, integrating with Azure Synapse through Synapse Link. Server-side latency is a key operational metric monitored for the service. This combination of features makes it a comprehensive platform for resource management, data replication, and diverse workload support across global deployments.

Container Registry
Azure Container Registry is a service for hosting container images, supporting geo-replication, zone redundancy, image locking, and private endpoints.

Azure API Management
Azure API Management is an Azure service for publishing, securing, transforming, and monitoring APIs. It functions as an API gateway and management platform, enabling organizations to expose APIs to external clients and different application teams. It is relevant to mission-critical application ingress as an application delivery service. The service offers multiple tiers, including the Consumption tier and Premium v2 tier, and provides architecture best practices with refactored guidance for improved clarity and usability.

Azure Functions
Azure Functions is a serverless compute platform where application logic runs as distinct functions in response to events.<SEP>Azure Functions is a serverless compute service that provides event-driven execution with multiple hosting options.<SEP>Azure Functions is a service that can bind to the Azure Cosmos DB change feed to process items into storage for custom backups.<SEP>Azure Functions is a serverless compute service on Azure.<SEP>Azure's serverless compute service.

Azure Logic Apps
Azure Logic Apps is a serverless platform for creating automated workflows using a graphical user interface with built-in triggers.<SEP>Azure Logic Apps is a cloud service for automating workflows with multiple deployment modes.

Power Apps
Power Apps provides a low-code/no-code development experience with workflow logic configurable through a user interface.<SEP>Power Apps is a low-code platform for building business applications.

Power Automate
Power Automate provides low-code/no-code workflow automation with integrations configurable through connections.<SEP>Power Automate is a service for automating workflows across applications and services.

Serverless Computing
Serverless computing provides resources on demand, eliminating infrastructure management, with automatic provisioning and scaling.

Microsoft Entra
Microsoft Entra provides authentication for Azure Container Registry.<SEP>Microsoft Entra provides integrated authentication for pushing and pulling container images.<SEP>Microsoft Entra provides identity and role-based access control (RBAC) for Azure Cosmos DB authentication and resource management.<SEP>Microsoft Entra provides authentication to connect to services without using connection strings or keys.<SEP>Microsoft Entra provides custom roles used to limit authorization for permanently deleting secrets, keys, and certificates in Key Vault.<SEP>Microsoft Entra provides activity logs that can be exported to Log Analytics Workspace for monitoring and retention.

Premium Plan
The Premium plan is a recommended Azure Functions hosting option that allows configuring compute instance size for maximizing reliability and performance.

Zone Redundancy
Zone redundancy in the Premium Container Registry tier provides protection against availability zone failures.

Azure Virtual Machines
Azure Virtual Machines serve as the primary IaaS application hosting model for constrained migrations from on-premises deployments.<SEP>Azure Virtual Machines are IaaS VMs provided by Azure for application hosting, requiring management of operating systems and software packages.<SEP>Azure Virtual Machines and scale sets have updated architecture best practices reflecting new Azure features.<SEP>Azure's compute service for virtual machines and scale sets.<SEP>Azure Virtual Machines and Scale Sets are compute services with architecture best practices.

Image Locking
Image locking prevents changes or deletions to container image versions or repositories in Container Registry.

Dedicated Plan
The Dedicated plan is the least serverless Azure Functions hosting option, providing autoscale but with slower scale operations than other plans.

Web Application Firewall
A web application firewall (WAF) provides protection for HTTP endpoints from common external attack vectors when using Azure Functions HTTP triggers.<SEP>Web Application Firewall (WAF) provides protection from common web exploits and vulnerabilities such as SQL injection.<SEP>Web Application Firewall provides protection against common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting.

Private Endpoints
Private endpoints restrict access to private virtual networks and help prevent unauthorized access, mitigating data exfiltration risks.<SEP>Private Endpoints provide private connectivity to Azure platform services within a virtual network.<SEP>Private Endpoints are a security convention enforced via Azure Policy, used to connect to services like Azure Key Vault.<SEP>Private Endpoints are a security convention that can be enforced through Azure Policy.<SEP>Private endpoints provide private connectivity to Azure services as part of Azure Private Link.

Azure App Service
Azure App Service is a cloud platform service provided by Microsoft Azure for hosting web applications, APIs, and containerized workloads. It serves as a low-friction container platform and an alternative to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), offering similar capabilities without the complexity of Kubernetes management.

Azure App Service includes features such as Auto Heal, Health Check, and availability zone configuration. Health Checks support scale-out operations and enable recycling of unhealthy instances. The platform provides secondary deployment slots that can be swapped after a deployment, facilitating zero-downtime releases.

Azure App Service operates as a multitenant environment with a limited number of outbound ports available per instance. It also has IPv6 support considerations and established architecture best practices for optimal use.

Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets provide automatic scaling, health monitoring, and automatic repair of unhealthy instances.<SEP>Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets enable deployment and management of groups of VMs with features like automatic instance repairs, flexible orchestration, and fault domain management.

Auto Heal
Auto Heal automatically recycles unhealthy workers to enable self-healing for mission-critical applications.<SEP>Auto Heal is a feature for Azure App Service Linux that automatically mitigates issues by recycling instances.

Azure Container Registry
Azure Container Registry is a service for storing and managing container images with geo-replication and vulnerability scanning capabilities.<SEP>Azure Container Registry is a native Azure service for hosting container images, supporting geo-replication, Microsoft Entra authentication, and automated container building.<SEP>Azure Container Registry is an Azure service for storing and managing container images.<SEP>Azure Container Registry is a service for storing and managing container images, supporting geo-replication, zone redundancy, private endpoints, and image locking.<SEP>Azure Container Registry is a container image registry where old image versions should be automatically purged.<SEP>Azure Container Registry is an Azure service that stores container images, supporting auto-purge of old versions.

Microsoft
Microsoft is the technology company that provides the Azure cloud platform and its related services. It offers Azure-native toolsets, including GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines, for deploying and managing mission-critical applications. Microsoft operates the backbone network over which Azure Front Door forwards requests and maintains Azure IP Ranges and Service Tags. The company also provides the Zero Trust security model and Entra identity services. Microsoft continues to invest in future platform capabilities across the Azure ecosystem.<SEP>Microsoft is the organization behind Azure and the Well-Architected Framework.<SEP>Microsoft offers the Azure Well-Architected Review and the Well-Architected Framework.

Health Check
Health Check identifies non-responsive workers by assessing critical downstream dependencies.<SEP>Health Check is a feature for monitoring App Service instances' health status.

Geo-Replication
Geo-replication is a method to replicate container images across all regions in Azure Container Registry.<SEP>Geo-replication is a capability of Azure Container Registry that replicates images to multiple regions, providing resiliency against regional outages and reducing latency.<SEP>Geo-replication is a Container Registry feature for replicating container images across multiple Azure regions for high availability.<SEP>Geo-replication is a method for deploying cache instances across different Azure regions in active-active configuration to maximize availability.

App Service Plan
An App Service plan defines the set of compute resources for App Service, with configurable scaling rules, instance limits, and availability zone support.<SEP>App Service Plan defines the compute resources and scaling for apps hosted in Azure App Service.

Microsoft Entra ID
Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft's identity platform that serves as a global, shared foundational service and a platform dependency for almost all Azure services. It provides centralized identity management, authentication, and authorization capabilities, offering an alternative to connection strings and keys for securing access to Azure resources.

Microsoft Entra ID delivers centralized account management, application access management, and enhanced identity protection. It supports role-based access control (RBAC) through service principals and service connections, including integration with Azure DevOps. It is used for managing access to services such as Azure Container Registry and provides integration with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) for centralized identity and access management.<SEP>Microsoft Entra ID is an authentication service used with Azure Service Bus for secure access.<SEP>Microsoft Entra ID is an identity service integrated with multiple Azure services for authentication and authorization.

Containerization
Containerization is an abstraction layer for application code and dependencies, enabling portability and consistent execution across platforms.

Microsoft Defender For Container Registries
Microsoft Defender for container registries provides vulnerability scanning for container images.<SEP>Microsoft Defender for container registries provides security scanning for container images.

Composite SLO
Composite SLO is a reliability metric calculated across user flows and deployment regions, with targets aligned to business requirements.<SEP>Composite SLO defines combined service level objective targets for reliability.

Content Delivery Network
A Content Delivery Network (CDN) minimizes network latency for distributed user bases through edge caching.<SEP>A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a distributed content caching service that Azure Front Door's built-in cache can replace in many use cases.<SEP>A Content Delivery Network (CDN) serves static content; Azure Front Door's built-in cache can eliminate the need for a dedicated CDN in many use cases.<SEP>A CDN serves static content from edge nodes; Azure Front Door's built-in cache may eliminate the need for a dedicated CDN.

Recovery Point Objectives
RPO defines the acceptable amount of data loss measured in time during a disaster.

Recovery Time Objectives
RTO defines the acceptable downtime duration for recovering a service after a failure.

Regional Pairs
Azure regional pairs consist of two regions in a single geography, used to ensure business continuity and protection against data loss.<SEP>Regional pairs are Azure region pairings that benefit from serialized deployment (SDP) rollouts for planned maintenance and regional prioritization for unplanned maintenance.

Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is a managed Kubernetes container orchestration service provided by Microsoft Azure that enables quick cluster provisioning. It serves as an application hosting platform, notably used in baseline mission-critical architectures.

AKS offers advanced networking capabilities, including support for network policies, multiple networking models, Azure CNI static block allocation, and HTTP proxy support. It also provides features for identity management, reliability, custom certificate authority integration, and node pool configuration.

The service supports deployment strategies such as blue/green deployments through separate pod deployments on each node and service definition updates. AKS requires regular Kubernetes version updates and comes with architecture best practices guidance.

Azure Container Apps
Azure Container Apps is an Azure platform for container management.<SEP>Azure Container Apps is an Azure container hosting service.<SEP>Azure Container Apps is an Azure service with architecture best practices covering security, performance, and cost optimization.<SEP>Azure Container Apps is a serverless container service with architecture best practices.

Linux-Based Container Runtimes
Linux-based container runtimes are recommended for containers due to lightweight images and frequent feature releases.

Cluster Autoscaler
Cluster autoscaler automatically adjusts the number of agent nodes in response to resource constraints.

Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
Horizontal pod autoscaler adjusts the number of pods in a deployment based on CPU utilization or other metrics.

AKS Uptime SLA
AKS Uptime SLA provides Kubernetes API endpoint availability guarantees for production clusters.

Microsoft Entra Workload ID
Microsoft Entra Workload ID enables managed identities at the pod level in AKS.<SEP>Microsoft Entra Workload ID provides managed identities for Azure Kubernetes Service workloads.<SEP>Microsoft Entra Workload ID provides workload identity capabilities for AKS.

AKS Security Baseline
AKS security baseline provides configuration guidance for ensuring a suitable security posture for mission-critical scenarios.

Kubernetes RBAC
Kubernetes RBAC is used with Microsoft Entra ID for least privilege access control in AKS clusters.<SEP>Kubernetes RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) is used with Microsoft Entra ID to enforce least privilege access in AKS clusters.

Virtual Nodes
Virtual nodes provide extensive and rapid scale for high scale and burst scenarios in AKS.

IaaS
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is a cloud computing model using virtual machines as the primary application hosting model.

Proximity Placement Groups
Proximity placement groups minimize internode latency when colocation latency is a concern in AKS deployments.<SEP>Proximity placement groups reduce latency by co-locating AKS resources physically close together.<SEP>Proximity Placement Groups enable submillisecond latency between services by co-locating resources.

PaaS
PaaS (Platform as a Service) is a cloud service model that may have limitations for legacy or proprietary development software.<SEP>Platform as a Service (PaaS) is a cloud service model with lower operational costs and complexity compared to IaaS.

Azure Marketplace
Azure Marketplace provides standard images for VM deployment.<SEP>Azure Marketplace provides standard images for virtual machines.

North Star Architecture
The North Star architecture is the recommended cloud-native baseline pattern for mission-critical workloads.

Flexible Orchestration
Flexible orchestration in scale sets protects against failures by automatically distributing VMs across fault domains.

Mission-Critical Workloads
Mission-Critical Workloads are applications and systems that require high reliability, high availability, and minimal downtime. On Azure, they are designed to maximize reliability so applications remain performant and available, with emphasis on disaster recovery and fast failure recovery.

The design methodology for Mission-Critical Workloads focuses on zero-downtime deployments, automation, and rapid failure recovery. Baseline architectures recommend following cloud-native patterns, including containerization and container orchestration. Specific data platform and architecture pattern considerations are also important, and the workloads may have varying business requirements that influence design decisions.

Chaos Experiments
Chaos experiments inject application faults into VM components to observe and validate fault mitigation capabilities.<SEP>Chaos experiments involve injecting faults to validate application resilience, run alongside load tests.

Active/Passive
Active/passive is a deployment strategy suitable for scenarios with lower reliability targets.

Azure Safe Deployment Practice Framework
The Azure SDP framework ensures code and configuration changes undergo phased rollout with health analysis across regional pairs.<SEP>Azure Safe Deployment Practice (SDP) framework is a set of practices for advancing safe deployments on Azure.

Azure Geo-Redundant Storage
Azure GRS automatically replicates data to a secondary paired region, ensuring data durability if the primary region is not recoverable.

Azure Monitor
Azure Monitor is a comprehensive monitoring service provided by Microsoft Azure, enabled by default for all Azure subscriptions. It supports three core types of observability data: logs, metrics, and distributed traces, collecting operational data from a wide range of Azure resources.

Azure Monitor collects metrics, logs, and diagnostics across services such as Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure Cache for Redis. For AKS, it provides container insights with built-in Prometheus support. For Azure Cosmos DB, it gathers key metrics and diagnostic logs, including provisioned throughput, enabling near real-time operational insights and evaluation of database usage and sizing. It also evaluates health and key metrics for Azure Cache for Redis.

Azure Monitor provides an extensive alerting framework to detect, categorize, and respond to operational signals through Action Groups, supporting alerts, diagnostics, and observability across Azure resources. It integrates with Azure Dashboards for operational data visualization and supports Application Insights, with pricing based on data volume ingested and retention duration.<SEP>Azure Monitor is used to define alerts for unexpected key, certificate, and secret usage.<SEP>Azure Monitor provides health models with built-in alerting, visualizations, and easy integration for health modeling.

Compute Decision Tree
The Compute decision tree is an Azure architecture guide for selecting appropriate compute services.

Azure Policy
Azure Policy is a governance service within the Azure Resource Manager control plane that enforces organizational standards, security, and reliability conventions across Azure resources. It supplements Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) by restricting actions that authorized users can perform, providing centralized governance safeguards and compliance enforcement.

Azure Policy offers a framework for enforcing and auditing security and reliability baselines, ensuring compliance with engineering criteria. It remediates or prohibits configuration deviations at configuration-time, automates management activities, and provides compliance reporting for Azure resources. It is used to enforce compliance for mission-critical workloads.

Azure Policy provides built-in policy definitions for governing specific Azure services. For example, it offers centralized governance safeguards for AKS clusters, controlling pod functions and establishing reliability and security baselines. It also provides built-in policy definitions for Azure Cosmos DB, such as disabling key-based metadata write access. Additionally, Azure Policy is used to ensure all regional resources route operational data to the correct Log Analytics workspace.<SEP>Azure Policy is a governance service recommended for use with Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL.

Azure CNI
Azure CNI is a network plugin for AKS that enables Azure or Calico network policies for controlling traffic within clusters.<SEP>Azure CNI is a container networking interface for AKS that provides advanced networking capabilities.<SEP>Azure CNI is a network plugin for AKS network integration that supports a richer feature set.<SEP>Azure CNI is a robust and scalable network plugin recommended for most AKS scenarios.<SEP>An advanced AKS networking model where nodes, pods, and services receive IP addresses from the same virtual network.

Global Traffic Routing
Global traffic routing is a networking pattern for directing traffic across globally distributed deployments.<SEP>Global traffic routing is the practice of distributing traffic across multiple active regional deployment stamps using global routing services.

TCP Port Exhaustion
TCP port exhaustion occurs when the sum of outbound connections from a given App Service worker exceeds capacity.<SEP>TCP port exhaustion occurs when outbound connections from a worker exceed capacity, depending on worker size.

Docker Hub
Docker Hub is a public container registry that can lead to issues related to service availability, throttling, and data exfiltration.

Log Analytics
Log Analytics is an Azure service used for collecting, ingesting, and querying operational log data from Azure resources. It serves as a destination for both application-level and platform-level diagnostic logs. A Log Analytics workspace receives Azure Monitor operational data for Azure Cosmos DB and other global resources.

Log Analytics has operational limits, including concurrent query limits and daily ingestion caps, which may require optimization. Its exported data can be queried via Synapse Spark and used as a source for analytical workloads, including ingestion into Azure Synapse for AIOps analysis.<SEP>Log Analytics workspace serves as a global unified data sink for operational data exposed by Azure Front Door.<SEP>Log Analytics is an Azure monitoring service with expanded guidance for workspaces and ingestion-time transformation to reduce costs.<SEP>Log Analytics is an Azure monitoring service with architecture best practices.

Azure Event Hubs
Azure Event Hubs is used to route diagnostic logs to third-party tools.<SEP>Azure Event Hubs is an export destination for Log Analytics workspace data, required to be in the same region as the workspace.<SEP>Azure Event Hubs is a streaming platform that can receive exported Log Analytics data on a continuous or scheduled basis.<SEP>Azure Event Hubs is a messaging service with best practices for operational excellence, performance efficiency, and cost control.<SEP>Azure Event Hubs is an Azure messaging service with support for geo-replication and custom dead-letter queues.<SEP>Azure's event streaming platform.<SEP>Azure Event Hubs is a big data streaming platform with architecture best practices.

App Service
Azure App Service is a cloud platform for hosting web applications with features like autoscaling, per-app scaling, and diagnostic logging.

Container Registry Tasks
Container Registry tasks enable automated container building and patching in Azure Container Registry.

Autoscale
Autoscale ensures adequate resources are available by scaling out when any rule in a profile is met and scaling in when all rules are met.<SEP>Autoscale automatically adjusts throughput between 10% and 100% of a configured maximum based on application load, protecting against throttling errors.<SEP>Autoscale can be configured through runbook automation to ensure elasticity in response to changing traffic patterns for Azure Database for MySQL/PostgreSQL.<SEP>Autoscale is a feature that automatically provisions throughput in Azure Cosmos DB.

Per-App Scaling
Per-app scaling allows an application to scale independently from the App Service plan that hosts it.

Kubernetes
Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform with RBAC, metrics API, and version release cycles.<SEP>Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform where secrets can be injected as environment variables into deployments or Kubernetes secrets.

Azure Policy Add-On For AKS
The Azure Policy Add-on for AKS provides built-in policies to control pod functions like root privileges and enforce policy conformance.

Calico
Calico is a network policy option usable with Azure CNI for controlling traffic within AKS clusters.<SEP>Calico is a network policy implementation with a richer feature set and broader community adoption and support.<SEP>A network policy plugin for AKS with a richer feature set including Windows node support and both Azure CNI and Kubenet compatibility.

Prometheus
Prometheus provides metrics integration within Azure Monitor for AKS container insights.

SNAT Port Exhaustion
SNAT port exhaustion is a common failure scenario in App Service when outbound connections to public IP addresses exceed available SNAT ports.<SEP>SNAT port exhaustion occurs when large numbers of outbound requests deplete available source NAT ports, preventing new outbound connections.

Planned Maintenance
Planned Maintenance allows defining maintenance windows for AKS node and cluster update operations.

Auto-Upgrade Channels
Auto-upgrade channels automatically upgrade AKS clusters to newer versions of Kubernetes or newer node images when available.

Global Resources
Global resources are long-living, globally distributed resources shared across regions, responsible for traffic distribution, permanent state storage, and monitoring.

Regional Stamp Resources
Regional stamp resources are ephemeral, stateless resources deployed within a stamp that participate in completing business transactions and can be added or removed dynamically.

Core Architecture Pattern
The core architecture pattern is a design approach for mission-critical applications consisting of global resources, regional stamp resources, and regional resources.

Regional Resources
Regional resources are deployed in a region and outlive stamp resources, such as observability resources monitoring at the regional level.

North Star Design Approach
The north star design approach is a recommended design methodology for starting mission-critical architecture design on Azure.

Baseline With Network Controls
An extension of the baseline architecture that provides strict network controls to prevent unauthorized public access to workload resources.

Baseline Architecture
The baseline architecture is a reference for mission-critical applications accessed over public endpoints without private network connectivity requirements.

Baseline In Azure Landing Zones
An architecture for deploying mission-critical workloads in enterprise setups requiring integration with centralized shared services and on-premises connectivity.

Azure Landing Zones
Azure landing zones provide a subscription model within enterprise management groups for deploying workloads with centralized shared services.<SEP>Standardized environments in Azure including platform and application landing zones for deploying workloads.<SEP>Azure landing zones are a governed platform to help with onboarding workload teams, including platform landing zones and application landing zones.

Well-Architected Assessment
The Well-Architected Assessment is a review tool for self-assessing the readiness of mission-critical workloads in production, organized to check alignment to best practices for resiliency, reliability, and availability.

Mission-Critical Design Methodology
The mission-critical design methodology provides foundational design principles for checking design choices of a workload's architecture and end-to-end operational approach.<SEP>A design methodology underpinned by five key design principles that serve as a compass for design decisions across critical design areas.

Azure Cosmos DB SDK
The Azure Cosmos DB SDK provides built-in error handling, retry, and reliability capabilities.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB SDK provides client libraries with best practices and retry logic for application development.

Direct Connection Mode
Direct connection mode optimizes network performance through direct TCP connectivity to backend Azure Cosmos DB nodes.

CQRS
CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) is a pattern used to optimize data throughput.<SEP>CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) is an architectural pattern for asynchronous non-blocking messaging to load-level throughput.<SEP>Command and Query Responsibility Segregation is a pattern for load-leveling through asynchronous non-blocking messaging.<SEP>CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) is an architectural pattern for separating read and write operations.

Partitioning Strategy
A partitioning strategy optimizes data distribution across logical and physical partitions according to the data model.

Event Sourcing
Event Sourcing is a persistence pattern used alongside CQRS to optimize throughput.<SEP>Event Sourcing is an architectural pattern used for asynchronous non-blocking messaging.<SEP>Event Sourcing is a pattern used alongside CQRS for asynchronous updates to Azure Cosmos DB.<SEP>Event Sourcing is an architectural pattern for storing state changes as a sequence of events.<SEP>Event Sourcing is an architecture pattern for capturing state changes as a sequence of events.

Azure Security Baseline
Azure Security Baseline provides control guidance for Azure Cosmos DB backup and recovery.<SEP>Azure Security Baseline provides security recommendations for Azure Cosmos DB including backup and recovery guidelines.

Indexing
Indexing in Azure Cosmos DB is crucial for performance, using index exclusions to reduce RU/s and storage requirements.<SEP>Indexing in Azure Cosmos DB allows efficient querying of data.

Automatic Failover
Automatic failover is a feature for single write region configurations based on a defined failover priority considering all read region replicas.<SEP>Automatic failover is recommended for single write region Azure Cosmos DB deployments to handle write region outages.<SEP>Automatic failover ensures continuity of Azure Cosmos DB service during regional outages.

Continuous Backups
Continuous backups provide fine granularity of recovery points across the last 30 days for Azure Cosmos DB.

Multi-Region Write
Multi-region write is a data platform design pattern where changes to separate writeable replicas are synchronized and merged between all replicas with conflict resolution.<SEP>Multi-region write is an Azure Cosmos DB configuration where a write replica exists in each deployment region to reduce latency and provide maximum redundancy.

Availability Zone Redundancy
Availability Zone redundancy ensures data replicas are placed across multiple availability zones to protect against zone failures within a region.<SEP>Availability Zone redundancy provides high availability support for Azure Cosmos DB across multiple availability zones.

Paxos Consensus Protocol
The Paxos consensus protocol is applied to achieve quorum across replicas within a region in Azure Cosmos DB.<SEP>The Paxos consensus protocol is applied within the hub region to achieve quorum across replicas for conflict resolution.

Azure Cosmos DB For NoSQL
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL is the first-party API providing the richest feature set, where new capabilities typically become available first.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL is an API that supports custom numerical properties for conflict resolution and custom resolution policies.

Last Write Wins
Last Write Wins is a standardized conflict resolution policy used in multi-region write contexts when the same data item is changed in two separate write-replicas.<SEP>Last Write Wins (LWW) is a conflict resolution policy that uses a time-synchronization clock protocol to resolve update conflicts by selecting the item with the highest timestamp value.<SEP>Last Write Wins (LWW) is the default conflict resolution policy in Azure Cosmos DB that uses a time-synchronization clock protocol to resolve conflicts by selecting the item with the highest timestamp value.

Gateway Connectivity Mode
Gateway mode provides HTTPS connectivity to frontend gateway nodes for Azure Cosmos DB.

Direct Connectivity Mode
Direct mode facilitates connectivity over TCP to backend Azure Cosmos DB replica nodes for improved performance with fewer network hops.

Azure Application Architecture Guide
The Azure Application Architecture Guide provides additional data-platform guidance including decision trees and criteria for choosing data stores.

Chaos Testing
Chaos testing is used to test and validate backup, restore capabilities, and failover operations within continuous delivery processes.<SEP>A testing method that injects faults into an application under load to understand how it responds to failures.<SEP>Chaos testing injects artificial failures into the system to evaluate how it reacts and validate the effectiveness of resiliency measures.<SEP>Chaos testing is a testing approach used alongside load testing within CI/CD processes to observe and validate application health using the health model.

Conflict Resolution
Conflict resolution addresses situations where the same data item is changed in two separate write replicas before either change can be replicated.

Customer-Managed Keys
Customer-managed keys require appropriate key management procedures to ensure availability, backup, and rotation.<SEP>Customer-managed keys are encryption keys managed by the customer, used when clear regulatory requirements stipulate their use.

Service-Managed Encryption Keys
Service-managed encryption keys are recommended to reduce management complexity when applying encryption to data platforms.

Azure Data Store Decision Tree
The Azure Data Store Decision Tree is a reference guide within the Azure Application Architecture Guide for choosing data stores.

Centralized Data Services
Centralized data services (Central IT DBaaS) introduce operational bottlenecks that hinder agility and should be avoided in mission-critical or business-critical contexts.

Soft-Delete Pattern
A pattern where records are flagged as deleted (e.g., IsDeleted) rather than explicitly removed, allowing changes to propagate through the change feed before TTL-based automatic deletion.<SEP>A pattern using a boolean property and TTL to handle deletes in the Azure Cosmos DB change feed, required until full-fidelity updates are available.

Time-To-Live
Time-To-Live (TTL) is a configuration for automatic expiration of data no longer required.<SEP>TTL is a setting that enables Azure Cosmos DB to automatically delete expired data after it has been reflected in the change feed.

Analytical Store
A column-format store in Azure Cosmos DB optimized for analytical queries, addressing ETL pipeline complexity and latency.<SEP>Analytical store is a column store for large-scale analytics on Azure Cosmos DB operational data.<SEP>Analytical Store is a feature of Azure Cosmos DB containers that can be enabled with analytical TTL configuration.

Continuous Backup Mode
Backup mode allowing point-in-time restore with one-second granularity within the last 30 days, with self-service restore capability.

Change Feed
The Azure Cosmos DB change feed provides a time-ordered feed of insert and update operations to data in a container, excluding deletes.<SEP>Change feed is a mechanism in Azure Cosmos DB that captures and propagates data record changes.<SEP>The Azure Cosmos DB change feed writes data to a separate storage facility and supports both continuous and periodic custom backups, though it doesn't yet reflect deletes.<SEP>Change feed provides a persistent record of changes to Azure Cosmos DB containers.

Periodic Backup Mode
Default backup mode with configurable intervals and retention periods, stored in Geo-Redundant Storage, requiring a support request for restore operations.

Geo-Redundant Storage
GRS is the default storage redundancy for periodic backups, replicated to a paired region.

Azure Cosmos DB For Mongodb
An Azure Cosmos DB API that supports continuous backup configuration.

Azure Cosmos DB For Nosql
An Azure Cosmos DB API that supports continuous backup configuration.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL offers the most comprehensive feature set, particularly for performance tuning.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL is an Azure service with updated architecture best practices.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL is an Azure service with updated best practices including recommendations for Microsoft Entra ID, private endpoints, Azure Policy, and Azure Advisor.

Locally-Redundant Storage
LRS is a storage redundancy option available for both periodic and continuous backup storage in Azure Cosmos DB.

Zone-Redundant Storage
ZRS is a storage redundancy option for backup storage in Azure Cosmos DB, available in regions supporting Availability Zones.

Point-In-Time Restore
PITR allows restoring Azure Cosmos DB data to a specific point in time with one-second granularity within continuous backup mode.<SEP>Point-in-time restore is an operational recovery method for severe configuration errors in Azure SQL Database.<SEP>Point-in-time restore is an operational playbook method to recover from severe configuration errors.

Cosmos DB Account Reader Role
An Azure role assignment required to configure backup storage redundancy for Azure Cosmos DB.

Request Units
Request Units per second (RU/s) are the measure of throughput provisioned in Azure Cosmos DB, billed per region.<SEP>Request Units (RUs) are the billing unit for Azure Cosmos DB, charged per region for replicated configurations.

Resource Locks
Resource Locks protect Azure Cosmos DB resources against incorrect modification or deletion, applying only to control plane operations.<SEP>Resource Locks prevent accidental deletion or modification of Azure Cosmos DB resources.<SEP>Resource locks are a mechanism to prevent Azure resources from being modified or deleted, recommended mainly for long-lived global resources rather than ephemeral regional resources.

Soft Delete
Soft Delete is a pattern where data records are flagged as deleted rather than explicitly removed, enabling inclusion in the change feed.<SEP>Soft Delete is a change feed design pattern in Azure Cosmos DB for handling deleted data.

Session
Session is the default and most widely used consistency level in Azure Cosmos DB.

Cosmos DB Account Reader
A built-in RBAC role enabling read-only access to Azure Cosmos DB resources.<SEP>Cosmos DB Account Reader is a built-in RBAC role for reading Azure Cosmos DB account data.

DocumentDB Account Contributor
A built-in RBAC role enabling management of Azure Cosmos DB accounts including keys and role assignments, but not data-plane access.<SEP>DocumentDB Account Contributor is a built-in RBAC role for contributing to Azure Cosmos DB accounts.

Cosmos DB Operator
A built-in RBAC role similar to DocumentDB Account Contributor but without ability to manage keys or role assignments.<SEP>Cosmos DB Operator is a built-in RBAC role for operating Azure Cosmos DB resources.

Azure SQL Analytics
Azure SQL Analytics provides near real-time operational insights for detection of reliability incidents in Azure SQL DB.<SEP>Azure SQL Analytics is a monitoring tool for analyzing data and creating alerts for Azure SQL databases.

Azure Synapse Analytics
Azure Synapse Analytics is a Microsoft analytics service with SQL Serverless pools and Spark pools that can query Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Store.<SEP>Azure Synapse Analytics is an analytics service providing unified experience through Azure Synapse Studio.

Command And Query Responsibility Segregation
CQRS is an architecture pattern that separates read and write operations.

Azure Cache For Redis
Azure Cache for Redis is an in-memory caching service based on open source Redis, offering Premium, Enterprise, and Enterprise Flash tiers with geo-replication and high availability capabilities.<SEP>Azure Cache for Redis is a caching service with features for connection resilience and scheduled updates.<SEP>Azure Cache for Redis had its service guide retired as the content was outdated.

Active Geo-Replication
Active Geo-Replication deploys readable replicas within all deployment regions, up to four.<SEP>Active Geo-Replication is a feature of Azure SQL Database that enables readable secondary databases in different regions.

Hyperscale (Citus)
Hyperscale (Citus) is a PostgreSQL deployment option providing dynamic scalability through sharding, with 99.95% SLA when High Availability is enabled.<SEP>Hyperscale (Citus) is a deployment option for Azure Database for PostgreSQL that provides dynamic scalability through sharding, with 99.95% SLA when High Availability is enabled.<SEP>Hyperscale (Citus) is a deployment option for Azure Database For PostgreSQL that maximizes availability across multiple nodes with High Availability mode offering 99.95% SLA.<SEP>Hyperscale (Citus) is a PostgreSQL-based distributed database option on Azure supporting sharding and reserved pricing.

Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Store
Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Store applies a column format for optimized analytical queries with multi-region availability.<SEP>A fully isolated column-oriented data store that enables large-scale analytics on Azure Cosmos DB data without impacting transactional workloads, with auto-sync latency usually under two minutes.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Store is an optimized column store for performing analytics on operational data without impacting transactional performance.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Store is a column store enabling analytical queries on operational data in Azure Cosmos DB.

Query Performance Insights
Query Performance Insights optimizes queries, tables, and databases in Azure SQL Database.<SEP>Query Performance Insights is a tool for Azure SQL Database that helps identify and analyze query performance issues.

Azure SQL Database
Azure SQL Database is a fully managed relational database service offered by Microsoft on the Azure cloud platform. It is a mature relational database engine recommended for relational data requirements, providing a wide range of reliability, security, and performance capabilities.

Azure SQL Database supports high availability features including availability zones, zone redundancy, geo-replication, auto failover groups, and automated backups, offering up to a 99.995% SLA. It also supports sharding for horizontal scaling.

The service includes comprehensive guidance and best practices covering architecture design, connection pooling, performance optimization, cost optimization, secure data storage, and immutable storage for audit logs.

Azure Synapse Spark
Azure Synapse Spark is a Spark-based analytics engine within Azure Synapse Analytics used to query and process data.

Azure Cosmos DB Change Feed
A feature of Azure Cosmos DB that can be used to maintain a separate secondary data store for analytical scenarios.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB change feed can maintain a separate secondary data store for analytical scenarios.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB change feed is a feature that provides a log of changes to items in a container.<SEP>Azure Cosmos DB change feed provides a mechanism for tracking changes in Azure Cosmos DB.

Azure Database For PostgreSQL
Azure Database For PostgreSQL is a managed relational database offered in Single Server, Flexible Server, and Hyperscale (Citus) deployment options.<SEP>Azure Database for PostgreSQL is a managed database service on Azure offering Single Server, Flexible Server, and Hyperscale (Citus) deployment options.<SEP>Azure Database For PostgreSQL is a managed database service offering Flexible Server and Hyperscale (Citus) options for business critical workloads.<SEP>Azure Database for PostgreSQL is a managed PostgreSQL database service on Azure.<SEP>Azure's managed PostgreSQL database service.<SEP>Azure Database for PostgreSQL is a managed PostgreSQL database service with architecture best practices.

Flexible Server
Flexible Server is a deployment option offering Availability Zone redundancy with 99.99% SLA, cost efficiencies through stop/start capability, and burstable compute tier.<SEP>Flexible Server is a deployment option for Azure Database For PostgreSQL recommended for business critical workloads due to Availability Zone support.

Caching For Hot Tier Data
An in-memory caching layer concept that enhances data platforms by increasing read throughput and improving response times for hot tier data scenarios.

Azure Synapse
Azure Synapse is an enterprise analytical platform combining relational and non-relational data with Spark technologies and built-in Azure service integration for big data analytics.<SEP>Azure Synapse is an enterprise analytical platform that combines relational and non-relational data with Spark technologies, including SQL data warehousing, Spark big data, and Data Explorer capabilities.<SEP>Azure Synapse brings together SQL data warehousing, Spark big data, and Data Explorer for log and time series analytics.<SEP>Azure Synapse Analytics is an analytical platform offering ML capabilities, Spark Pools, notebooks, and native integration with Azure Data Factory for AIOps and predictive action.<SEP>Azure Synapse is an analytics service used for ingesting and analyzing Log Analytics operational data.<SEP>Azure Synapse is an Azure analytics service.

Enterprise Flash Tier
The Enterprise Flash tier of Azure Cache for Redis runs on a combination of RAM and flash non-volatile memory, enabling very large cache sizes up to 13TB with clustering.

Analytical Scenarios
Analytical scenarios drive additional value from data flows and require different data platform capabilities optimized for read queries and aggregations over large data volumes.

Transactional
Transactional workloads process large volumes of individual transactions, optimized for near real-time CRUD queries with row-based storage.

AIOps
AIOps refers to application and operational analytical scenarios that form a crucial aspect of a highly reliable data platform.<SEP>AIOps refers to models that analyze and correlate application observability data from various environments.<SEP>AIOps applies AI methodologies in CI/CD pipelines to detect potential regressions or degradations and preemptively stop deployments.<SEP>AIOps (AI Operations) is a methodology applying machine learning to correlate and prioritize operational data, enabling detection, diagnosis, and prediction of system issues.<SEP>AIOps refers to the use of artificial intelligence for IT operations, involving ML model training on operational data for predictive and automated insights.<SEP>AIOps is the use of AI to continually improve operational procedures and triggers.

Single Server
Single Server is a deployment option for Azure Database for PostgreSQL with 99.99% SLA.

Sharding
Sharding distributes data and processing across multiple identical structured databases by partitioning horizontally.<SEP>Sharding partitions relational databases based on different application and data contexts to maximize scalability, availability, and fault isolation.

Business-Critical Service Tier
The Business-Critical service tier maximizes reliability and availability with critical resiliency capabilities for Azure SQL Database.

Auto Failover Groups
Auto Failover Groups replicate databases to a secondary server and allow transparent failover upon failure.<SEP>Auto Failover Groups provide transparent failover to a secondary region with geo-replication for read optimization and database redundancy.

Transparent Data Encryption
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) provides server-side at-rest encryption for Azure SQL Database.

Zone-Redundant Deployment Model
The Zone-Redundant deployment model spreads Business Critical database replicas within the same region across Availability Zones.

Reserved Capacity
Reserved Capacity provides potential cost optimizations for Azure SQL Database and Azure Database for PostgreSQL compute costs.

Azure Synapse Studio
Azure Synapse Studio provides a unified experience for ingestion and querying tasks.<SEP>Azure Synapse Studio is the unified experience interface for Azure Synapse Analytics.

Azure Storage
Azure Storage is used for 'cold' operations data for analytical purposes.<SEP>Azure Storage can be used as a target for custom backup implementations from Azure Cosmos DB.<SEP>Azure Storage is a cloud storage service used as a data source and workspace storage for analytical scenarios.<SEP>Azure Storage is an export destination for Log Analytics workspace data, supporting various redundancy levels including ZRS and GRS.<SEP>Azure Storage in GRS configuration is recommended for long-term operational data storage exported from Log Analytics.<SEP>Azure Storage in GRS configuration is used to host custom visuals and plugins for Grafana.<SEP>Azure Storage is used for storing operational data, exported Log Analytics data, and prepared ML training data.

Azure Synapse Link
Azure Synapse Link provides an analytical store whose data is not included in Azure Cosmos DB backups.<SEP>Azure Synapse Link enables direct querying of Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Store from Azure Synapse, enabling no-ETL Hybrid Transactional-Analytical Processing (HTAP).<SEP>Azure Synapse Link connects Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Store to Azure Synapse for querying operational data without impacting transactional performance.<SEP>Azure Synapse Link enables connectivity between Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Synapse Analytics.

CAP Theorem
The CAP theorem expresses the trade-off between consistency and latency in distributed applications with multiple data replicas.<SEP>CAP theorem describes trade-offs between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance in distributed systems.

PACELC Theorem
The PACELC theorem expresses the trade-off between consistency and latency in distributed applications with multiple data replicas.<SEP>PACELC theorem extends CAP theorem to describe trade-offs including latency and consistency in distributed systems.

Azure Data Lake Gen2
Azure Data Lake Gen2 is a storage layer with hierarchical namespace, supported as an external store for Synapse queries.

SAGA
SAGA is a design pattern applied to manage consistency and dependencies between different datastores in a microservice architecture.<SEP>SAGA is a design pattern used where dependencies between datastores exist in microservice architectures.<SEP>SAGA is a distributed transaction pattern referenced in the architecture documentation.

Azure Data Factory
Azure Data Factory (ADF) is a batch-oriented orchestration service used to copy data from Azure Cosmos DB, supporting manual, schedule, tumbling window, and event-based triggers.<SEP>Azure Data Factory provides connectors for Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL and MongoDB API with schedule, tumbling window, and event-based triggers.<SEP>Azure Data Factory supports copy activity with various supported data stores and formats.<SEP>Azure Data Factory provides ETL tools natively integrated with Azure Synapse for data extraction, transformation, loading, and orchestration.<SEP>Azure Data Factory is an Azure data integration service.

Azure Private Link
Azure Private Link is supported by Azure Data Factory for high network security scenarios.<SEP>Azure Private Link enables private endpoint connections for secure access to services like Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Data Factory.<SEP>Azure Private Link provides dedicated access to Azure PaaS resources using private IP addresses and private network connectivity.<SEP>Azure Private Link enables private connectivity to Azure services through private endpoints.<SEP>Azure Private Link is referenced in networking guidance for Azure Virtual Desktop workloads.<SEP>Azure Private Link enables private connectivity to Azure services.

Event Grid
Event Grid is supported by Azure Data Factory for event-based triggers.

Single-Region Write
Single-region write is an Azure Cosmos DB configuration with globally distributed read replicas, offering 99.999% read SLA and 99.995% write SLA with Availability Zones.

Change Feed Processor
The change feed processor is a component that binds to the Azure Cosmos DB change feed to process items into storage.<SEP>Change feed processor is a library for consuming Azure Cosmos DB change feed.

ETL
Extract, Transform, and Load pipelines used to extract data into separate analytical platforms, consuming throughput and impacting transactional workload performance.<SEP>Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) is a traditional data processing approach that may not scale with deployment telemetry growth.

HTAP
Hybrid Transactional-Analytical Processing enables querying transactional data for analytics in near real-time without ETL.

Auto-Sync
The process where operational data changes are automatically synced to the Analytical Store, with latency usually less than two minutes.

Azure Synapse SQL Serverless Pools
SQL Serverless pools in Azure Synapse that can query the Analytical Store through automatically updated views or SELECT/OPENROWSET commands.

Azure Synapse Spark Pools
Spark pools in Azure Synapse that can query the Analytical Store through Spark tables or spark.read command, supporting dataframe operations and ML model training.

Request Unit
Request Units (RUs) represent throughput consumed by operations on Azure Cosmos DB; analytical queries on transactional data can consume significant RUs.

Caching Layer
A caching layer is used to increase read throughput and improve user experience and end-to-end client response times.

Microservice Architecture
A microservice architecture allows individual application services to be built with distinct scenario-optimized datastores rather than depending on a single monolithic datastore.<SEP>Microservice architecture is a loosely coupled application design principle where individual services use distinct data stores and scenario-optimized data technologies.

Apache Spark
Apache Spark is an analytical runtime environment that may have integration restrictions to analyze polyglot data structures.

Key Vault
Key Vault is a secure location for managing encryption keys, supporting both server-side and client-side encryption scenarios.<SEP>Key Vault is an Azure secret management solution providing zone and regional redundancy, and integration with Microsoft Entra ID.

Variety
Variety refers to considerations around data models, data types, data relationships, and query models that affect data platform decisions.<SEP>Variety is one of the Four Vs of Big Data, referring to the organization and format of data across structured, semi-structured, and unstructured formats.

MACsec
MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE MAC) is a data-link encryption method used to secure all traffic moving between Azure datacenters on the Microsoft backbone network.<SEP>MACsec is a data-link layer encryption method used on underlying network hardware to secure data in-transit between Azure data centers.

Veracity
Veracity refers to validating the accuracy of data within an application, encompassing consistency, security, governance, and change management.<SEP>Veracity is one of the Four Vs of Big Data, referring to data provenance, curation, governance, and quality assurance.

Volume
Volume refers to ensuring future data volumes do not exceed data platform capabilities, requiring capacity planning and monitoring.<SEP>Volume is one of the Four Vs of Big Data, referring to the size of the dataset and storage capacity requirements.

Client-Side Encryption
Client-side encryption is an encryption approach implemented in the application layer where keys can be managed in Key Vault or another secure location.

Polyglot Storage
Polyglot storage refers to the capability of analytical datastores to support various types of data structures.

Custom Resolution Policies
Custom resolution policies allow application-defined semantics to reconcile conflicts using a registered merge stored procedure, available only with Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL.

Recovery Time Objective
The RTO provided by Azure Cosmos DB is approximately 10-15 minutes for regional failover, with a strategic direction to reduce to approximately 5 minutes.<SEP>Recovery Time Objective (RTO) defines the target time to recover an application after failure.<SEP>Recovery time objective (RTO) is a target metric for how quickly operations should be restored after a failure.

Server-Side Encryption
Server-side encryption is an encryption approach implemented in the data layer using service-managed keys or customer-managed keys.

Recovery Point Objective
RPO is configurable via consistency levels, with a minimum of 0 for strong consistency with single-write region.<SEP>Recovery Point Objective (RPO) defines the acceptable amount of data loss measured in time.<SEP>Recovery point objective (RPO) defines the tolerance for data loss in disaster recovery scenarios.

Hub Region
The hub region is the primary region in Azure Cosmos DB's multi-region write configuration responsible for all conflict resolutions, determined by the first region configured.

Message Buffer
The message buffer stores write conflicts within the hub region to provide load leveling and redundancy, capable of storing a few minutes worth of write updates.

Consistency Levels
Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB are configurable settings that affect RPO, RTO, data durability, and throughput trade-offs, with five levels available.

Azure Traffic Manager
Azure Traffic Manager controls routing to specific gateway rings in Azure SQL Database.<SEP>Azure Traffic Manager is a globally distributed routing service with built-in multi-region redundancy and availability.<SEP>Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS redirection service that routes traffic based on configured rules without processing request payloads.<SEP>Azure Traffic Manager is a global routing service for non-HTTP/S scenarios, used as a replacement to Azure Front Door with different design considerations.<SEP>Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based traffic load balancing service.<SEP>Azure Traffic Manager is an Azure service with enhanced health probing and failover practices.<SEP>Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based traffic load balancer with architecture best practices.

Standard Throughput
Standard throughput allocates fixed resources to guarantee a specified RU/s value, billed hourly for provisioned throughput.

Consistency Level
Consistency level defines the data consistency guarantees offered by Azure Cosmos DB.

Dedicated Gateway
Dedicated Gateway is a connection mode feature of Azure Cosmos DB.

Periodic Backup
Periodic backup provides scheduled backup with zone-redundant or locally-redundant storage options, restored via support request.

Role-Based Access Control
RBAC provides built-in and custom roles for controlling access to Azure Cosmos DB resources.<SEP>Role-based access control is used to delegate incremental firewall policies to application security teams for policy autonomy.

Azure Function
Azure Function can be triggered by Azure Cosmos DB change feed.

Continuous Backup
Continuous backup enables point-in-time restore via Azure portal or ARM templates, with some limitations and additional storage cost.

Partition Key
Partition key selection is critical for optimal performance and data distribution in Azure Cosmos DB.

ARM Template
ARM Template is a method for configuring Azure Cosmos DB settings including RBAC, restore, and infrastructure as code deployments.

Stored Procedures
Stored procedures are server-side programmable logic that can be deployed in Azure Cosmos DB SQL database containers.

Triggers
Triggers are server-side logic executed before or after operations on Azure Cosmos DB containers.

MongoDB API
MongoDB API is an Azure Cosmos DB API that enables MongoDB-compatible access, supported by Azure Data Factory connector.

Conflict Resolution Policies
Conflict resolution policies handle update conflicts (insert, replace, delete) in Azure Cosmos DB multi-region writes.

UDFs
User-defined functions (UDFs) are custom functions that can be created in Azure Cosmos DB SQL database containers.

Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Column Store
Azure Cosmos DB Analytical Column Store is a data store component that separates transactional and analytical data in Azure Cosmos DB.

Spark Dataframe
Spark dataframe is used to load and query data from the analytical store.

Synapse Spark
Synapse Spark is a component of Azure Synapse Analytics used for querying data including Log Analytics exported data.

Data Tiering
Data tiering classifies datasets into 'hot', 'warm', and 'cold' tiers based on usage and criticality.

Multi-Region Data Platform
